h1: The 6 Best Blenders Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 6 best blenders under $200, from Ninja pitchers to nutribullet cups, compared on wattage, capacity and use case.
summary: The Ninja BN751 DUO is our top blender under $200 because it pairs a 72oz pitcher with two 24oz to-go cups. The Ninja Mega Kitchen System BL770 is the pick if you also want an 8-cup processor. The nutribullet Pro+ is for single-serve drinkers.
intro: The common mistake with a sub-$200 blender is buying on peak watts and ignoring what you will actually put in the jar. A 72oz pitcher is wasted on one morning smoothie, and a personal cup is hopeless for a family batch of soup or frozen drinks.

We ranked six blenders that all sit in the $100-200 price bucket, using wattage, container sizes and included functions from the spec sheets. We left out the pricier Ninja kitchen system because it falls above $200.

products.name: Ninja BN751 Professional Plus DUO Blender, 1400 Peak Watts, 72oz + 2x24oz Cups
products.verdict: A full pitcher and two to-go cups from one base.
products.description:
The BN751 offers 1400 peak watts, a 72oz pitcher and two 24oz to-go cups, plus 3 Auto-iQ programs. It covers both family batches and single servings.

It ranks above the BN701 because that model skips the personal cups. The tradeoff is a few more parts to store.

It suits households that blend in both sizes. The caveat is that the 1400 figure is peak watts, not continuous power.
products.idealFor: Households blending both batches and single servings.
products.skipIf: You only ever blend one large batch.

products.name: Ninja Mega Kitchen System, 1500W, 72oz Pitcher, 8-Cup, BL770
products.verdict: Blender and 8-cup food processor on one 1500W base.
products.description:
The BL770 has a 1500W motor, a 72oz pitcher and an 8-cup processor bowl on a dual-function base.

It ranks second because it gives up the Auto-iQ programs listed on the BN751 in exchange for the processor bowl. The extra power is the most in this ranking.

Choose it if you want one machine for blending and chopping. The caveat is a larger footprint on the counter.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want a blender and processor in one.

products.name: Ninja Professional Plus Blender, Auto-iQ, 1400W, 72oz Pitcher, BN701
products.verdict: Simple batch blending with Auto-iQ presets.
products.description:
The BN701 combines a 1400W motor with a 72oz pitcher and Auto-iQ preset programs.

It ranks below the BN751 since there are no personal cups, but above the BR201AMZ for more wattage. The tradeoff is single-purpose simplicity.

It fits households that only need batches. The caveat is nothing for to-go use.

products.name: nutribullet SmartSense Blender Combo, 1400W, 64oz Pitcher, 32oz & 24oz Cups
products.verdict: A pitcher-plus-cups setup outside the Ninja line.
products.description:
The SmartSense combo has a 1400W motor, a 64oz pitcher, 32oz and 24oz cups and 5-speed SmartSense control.

It ranks below the BN751 because the pitcher is smaller at 64oz and it lists no presets. The tradeoff is larger to-go cups and manual speed control.

A good choice for buyers who prefer nutribullet. The caveat is the smaller pitcher.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want pitcher and cups from nutribullet.

products.name: Ninja Professional Blender 2.0, 1200W, Auto-iQ, 72oz Pitcher, BR201AMZ
products.verdict: A 72oz pitcher with Auto-iQ and no extras.
products.description:
The BR201AMZ has a 1200W motor, a 72oz pitcher and Auto-iQ preset programs.

It ranks under the BN701 because it has 200W less power. The tradeoff is that the specs are otherwise similar.

It suits buyers who want power without extras. The caveat is no cups or processor.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a plain pitcher blender.

products.name: nutribullet Pro+ Personal Blender 1200W, 32oz & 24oz Cups
products.description:
The Pro+ is a personal blender with a 1200W motor, 32oz and 24oz cups, a pulse function and auto shut-off.

It ranks last because there is no pitcher, so batch jobs are out. The tradeoff is a smaller footprint.

Best for solo smoothies. The caveat is the lack of family-sized capacity.

whatMatters.detail: Watts describe motor power, and peak watts is a short burst figure. Higher power helps with ice and fibrous veg. Look for whether the listing says peak or continuous.
A 72oz pitcher serves a family, while 24oz and 32oz cups suit one person. Buying the wrong one wastes money. Check the listed capacities in ounces.
Auto-iQ is a preset that blends and pauses for you. It helps beginners get consistent results. Look for named presets in the title or bullets.
An 8-cup processor bowl lets one base chop and mix dough-like items. It saves buying a second appliance. Look for the cup size and whether the bowl is included.
Kitchen systems with extra parts need more storage. A tall pitcher may not fit under cabinets. Check the stated dimensions on the listing.

faq.a: Several Ninja listings state peak watts, which is a short burst rating. Read whether the figure is peak or continuous.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Buying a 72oz pitcher for single servings or a personal cup for family batches. Match the container to how many people you serve.

faq.q: Is the BL770 worth it over the BN751?
faq.a: If you want an 8-cup processor bowl, yes. If you want to-go cups and Auto-iQ programs, the BN751 is better.

faq.q: Do these come with to-go cups?
faq.a: The BN751, SmartSense combo and nutribullet Pro+ include cups. The BN701 and BR201AMZ are pitcher only.

faq.q: How should I clean a pitcher blender?
faq.a: Rinse right after use and check the manual for dishwasher safety. Avoid letting thick mixtures dry on the blade.

faq.q: Why is the Ninja kitchen system BN801 not included?
faq.a: Its price bucket is $200-500, above our $200 limit.

finalTake: The Ninja BN751 DUO is the best all-round blender under $200. The BL770 is the pick if you want processor duty, and the nutribullet Pro+ is right for solo smoothie drinkers. Match container size to your household and you will not overspend.
